claims.text: The AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock is cobalt-free.
In-situ substrate pre-heating during additive manufacturing will produce a more homogeneous AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
In-situ substrate pre-heating will lower residual stress in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
In-situ substrate pre-heating will reduce defects in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
The pre-heating intervention will improve the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi relative to fabrication without pre-heating.
Substrate pre-heating produces a refined and uniform microstructure.
Substrate pre-heating reduces thermal gradients during additive manufacturing.
Pre-heating reduces the temperature differential between the melt pool and the substrate.
Reducing the melt-pool-to-substrate temperature differential minimizes rapid thermal contraction.
Reducing the thermal differential suppresses compositional segregation during solidification.
Reducing the thermal differential lowers residual-stress buildup.
Reduced thermal contraction, segregation, and residual-stress buildup collectively limit defect formation.
Limiting defect formation improves overall mechanical integrity.
Pre-heated specimens will have enhanced tensile strength relative to specimens fabricated without pre-heating.
Pre-heated specimens will have enhanced ductility relative to specimens fabricated without pre-heating.
The magnitude of mechanical-property enhancement and stress reduction may depend on pre-heating temperature and other processing variables.

contradictions.description: The baseline and headline comparison include either conventional additive manufacturing or bulk fabrication, but the stated conditions, boundary, and falsification experiment compare only additive-manufactured samples with and without substrate pre-heating. Thus, the experiment cannot directly establish the claimed comparison with conventionally bulk-fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
